newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Von Moos sees break-even in 1997, ord loss.
newsitem.headline: Von Moos sees break-even in 1997, ord loss.

text.p: Swiss steel group Von Moos AG expects to cut its losses from ordinary activities to 25 million Swiss francs in 1997 from 53 million and to break even on the group level by dipping into reserves, its finance chief said.
In the text of a speech prepared for delivery at the company's annual news conference, Peter Kratz said sales were expected to rise to 700 million from 590 million.

Ordinary activities should reach the break-even point in 1998, he said, adding Von Moos wanted to post "an appropriate return on capital" in the year 2000. He said it would concentrate on core activity and sell off peripheral businesses.
